Category: Humanoid character.

Style: cardboard craft.

spec.name: Cardboard Box Robot Kid
spec.description: A 7-year-old kid in a homemade cardboard-box robot costume with a box head with a face window, a box torso with a hand-drawn control panel, foil-wrapped arm tubes, box shin guards and red gloves, standing in a T-pose.
spec.layout: Everything is a primitive-built paper-craft puppet standing on y=0, facing +Z, centred on x=0, about 1.2 m of kid plus 0.35 m of costume. Bottom to top: red-soled white sneakers on the floor (y 0 to 0.075), jeans legs, cardboard shin boxes (y 0.10 to 0.40, x 0.10 +/- 0.075, z +/- 0.085, wider than the legs inside), blue shirt hem and jeans waist (y 0.36 to 0.46), the torso box (y 0.42 to 0.90, x +/- 0.26, z -0.16 to 0.18), the head box (y 0.90 to 1.36, x +/- 0.22, z -0.18 to 0.20) and two spring antennas (up to y 1.56). The head box has a rectangular face window in front (x +/- 0.13, y 0.97 to 1.20, z 0.20). The kid's round cartoon head sits inside it (centre [0,1.08,0.04], radius 0.12), recessed 4 cm behind the window, so the face reads from the front: big eyes, brows, small nose, a wide grin with a separate lower jaw. The arms go out sideways in a T-pose at y 0.80, passing through torn holes in the torso sides (x +/- 0.26). Visible parts of each arm: blue shirt-sleeve elbow, red glove. Over the upper arm (x 0.27 to 0.43) and forearm (x 0.50 to 0.68) sit foil-wrapped cardboard tubes with tape rings. Between them the blue sleeve shows at the elbow (x 0.43 to 0.50). Red gloves start at the wrist (x 0.68) with separate fingers and thumb, palms down, thumb toward +Z, fingertips at x +/- 0.85. Legs stand shoulder-width apart (x +/- 0.10), straight, toes forward. The style is cardboard craft. Every box is a plain tan cuboid with chunky, visibly thick edges (about 1 cm slabs), cut flaps, torn edges and darker corrugation-rib strips along the cut edges. Silver tape strips cross the corners and seams. Hand-drawn marker details (black outlines, red and blue scribbles) are thin dark and coloured plates seated about 2 mm proud of the cardboard. Bottle caps (yellow, green) are buttons, white glue blobs sit at joins, and foil is crinkled with faceted flat-shaded facets in two greys. Colours are flat per part, warm tan on top faces and darker tan below. The kid parts are soft chunky shapes (round-ish, sphere/capsule based) that contrast with the hard box costume.

parts.builds: The kid's head and neck, seen through the box's face window. Chunky cartoon head (rounded boxy skull sphere, radius ~0.12, centre [0,1.08,0.04], skin). Neck cylinder from y 0.88 to 0.97 (skin) with a blue shirt collar ring (shirt) around its base. Face: two big eyes (white sclera, brown iris, tiny white highlight, thin dark marker-colour upper lid line) at x +/-0.045, y 1.10, front z about 0.15. Thick eyebrows (hair colour) angled up for a happy look. Small round nose (skin, slightly pinker via cheek) and round cheek blush discs (cheek) at x +/-0.075, y 1.04. Mouth: upper jaw is part of the head (lips-colour upper lip arc, row of white upper teeth); the lower jaw is a separate piece on the `jaw` joint (skin chin block, lips lower lip, white lower teeth, pink-red tongue in lips colour) forming a wide open-ish grin. Ears (skin, with cheek inner disc) at x +/-0.12. Hair (hair colour): a solid cap over the top and back of the head plus a modest number of overlapping broad blades for tousled bangs over the forehead and a cowlick, built big and clear; hair shows through the top of the window. Keep every feature behind z 0.185 so nothing pokes through the window plane at z 0.20.
parts.attaches: Neck base on mount neckBase (the neck rides joint neck, the skull and hair ride head, lower jaw rides jaw, hinge at jawHinge). Sits inside the headBox, whose window is at faceWindow; the neck passes down into the torsoBox top at torsoTop.

parts.builds: Every visible part of the kid except head and neck. Pelvis and lower torso: blue shirt hem block and a jeans waistband visible below the torso box (y 0.36 to 0.46) and a stub of shirt chest inside the box top (hidden). Legs: chunky jeans (jeans colour) capsules or sweeps on the chains hipL/kneeL/ankleL and hipR/kneeR/ankleR, radius ~0.05 thigh to 0.04 ankle, with small patch pockets, seam stitching strips and rolled cuffs. White sneakers on the toe/ankle joints (x +/-0.10, y 0 to 0.075, z -0.05 to 0.17): sneaker body, rounded toe cap, red sole slab (sole), laces as small crossing strips and a tongue, heel tab. Arms: blue shirt-sleeve tubes (shirt) on shoulder/elbow/wrist chains along y 0.80 from x +/-0.20 to +/-0.70, radius ~0.04, with soft cuffs at the wrists. Hands: red gloves (glove) from x +/-0.68, palm block about 0.10 wide in z and 0.06 along x, palm down, separate finger capsules on every digit joint (thumbL1/2, indexL1/2, middleL1/2, ringL1/2, pinkyL1/2 and the R mirror) so fingers and thumb are separated and extended, with a lighter white cuff band and a small marker-colour star or dot on the back of each glove. Mirror left/right exactly.
parts.attaches: Rides hips, spine, chest, shoulder/elbow/wrist/hand and digit joints, hip/knee/ankle/toe joints. Arms pass through the torso box side holes at shoulderHoleL/R and are covered by the limbSleeves tubes between upperArmTube and forearmTube mounts. Legs go through the shin boxes at shinBoxTop/Bottom mounts. Shoes sit on y=0.

parts.builds: The body of the costume: a large cardboard box (cardTan) x +/-0.26, y 0.42 to 0.90, z -0.16 to 0.18, built as thick wall slabs with visible edge thickness and darker corrugation-rib strips (cardDark) along cut edges. Open bottom hem and top with the head box sitting on the top face. Folded-over top flaps (cardLight inner faces, cardDark outer) around the neck opening. Side walls have rough torn round arm holes at shoulderHoleL/R (cardInside dark ring with jagged torn tabs) that the arms pass through. Front chest control panel at chestPanel: a lighter cardboard rectangle plate glued on (cardLight) with a marker outline (marker), a rectangular drawn screen (screenCyan plate, glowing, with marker zig-zag waveform and a small smiley), three big dial knobs (bottle caps: capYellow, capGreen, markerRed with marker tick lines), a row of 4 push-buttons, a toggle switch row (small rods with caps), two scribbled vent grilles (parallel marker bars), a kid-lettered 'ROBO' (blocky letter plates in markerBlue) and a name tag sticker (white plate with marker scribble). Silver tape strips (tapeSilver) cross all four vertical corners and a diagonal across one chest corner, with glue blobs (white). Back at backPanel: a small cardboard jetpack box with two foil tubes (foil/foilShade, faceted) and a red tape stripe, plus a hand-drawn gear. Belt at beltLine y 0.42 to 0.46: cardTan strip band around the box bottom with a big capYellow bottle-cap buckle and marker stitches. Nothing sticks out past z +0.26 front or z -0.26 back.
parts.attaches: Rides joint chest. Bottom edge at torsoBottom/beltLine, top face at torsoTop where headBox sits and kid neck enters. Arm holes at shoulderHoleL/R (x +/-0.26, y 0.8).

parts.builds: The robot head: a cardboard box x +/-0.22, y 0.90 to 1.36, z -0.18 to 0.20 (cardTan, thick wall slabs with cardDark corrugation ribs on edges). The front wall is built from four slabs around a rectangular face window (x +/-0.13, y 0.97 to 1.20, z 0.20) so the kid's face is visible, with a cut-edge frame in cardInside lining the opening, a hand-painted marker rim (marker, thin plates) around it and little yellow-marker lightning rivets in the corners. Tape strips (tapeSilver) over the top corners and a torn flap on the window top edge. Top face: folded-open flaps (cardLight inner, cardDark outer) on top and a silver tape cross. Two spring antennas at antennaBaseL/R (thin coil sweeps in foilShade, about 0.12 tall, tilted slightly outward) each ending in a bottle-cap or foil-ball tip (capYellow and markerRed), one at x +0.10 and one at x -0.10, topping out about y 1.56. Ear tubes at earTubeL/R: cardboard rolls (cardDark/cardLight rings) sticking out of each side wall to x +/-0.30, with foil end discs and a marker spiral. Front above the window: drawn eyebrow marker bars (marker) and two small round 'eye lights' (capGreen caps) as decoration, a mouth-grille of marker lines on the chin strip beneath the window (y 0.91 to 0.96). Sides and back have marker-drawn bolts, an arrow decal and a gear doodle. Glue blobs (white) at the seams.
parts.attaches: Rides joint head. Rests on torsoBox top at torsoTop (y 0.90). Face window centre at faceWindow around the kid's face from kidHead; keep the window opening empty.

parts.builds: Costume tubes and boxes on the kid's limbs, mirrored left/right. Arms: foil-wrapped cardboard tubes (foil with foilShade faceted creases as strips) as sweeps or rods around the sleeve, upper arm tube from x +/-0.27 to +/-0.43 (radius ~0.065) at upperArmTube and forearm tube from x +/-0.50 to +/-0.68 (radius ~0.06) at forearmTube, each with raised tapeSilver rings at both ends, a markerRed stripe, a few capYellow rivets/caps and glue blobs, torn cardboard edge cuffs (cardTan) at the wrist end and a cardDark inner ring. Between the tubes (x 0.43 to 0.50) only the kid's blue sleeve shows, with a small cardboard elbow guard disc (cardLight) beside it. The pieces ride shoulder/elbow joints appropriately (upper tube on shoulder joint, forearm tube on elbow joint). Legs: cardboard shin boxes (cardTan, thick wall slabs, open top and bottom, x 0.10 +/-0.075, z +/-0.085, y 0.10 to 0.40) on each leg, with cardDark corrugation ribs on the vertical edges, silver tape wraps on top and bottom, a folded flap collar at the top (cardLight inner), a marker-drawn arrow or lightning bolt on the front (markerBlue and marker), a capGreen bottle-cap 'knee light' on the front, and a foil-wrapped kneecap strip with tape ring at kneeL/R. Shin boxes ride kneeL/kneeR joints. Keep box bottoms at y 0.10 so shoes stay visible.
parts.attaches: Arm tubes wrap the arm sleeves at upperArmTubeL/R and forearmTubeL/R and start outside the torso hole at shoulderHoleL/R; they end at the wristL/R mounts where gloves begin. Shin boxes wrap the jeans between shinBoxBottom and shinBoxTop mounts around kneeL/R.

calls.reasoning:
I'm picturing a kid around 1.2 meters tall in a cardboard-box robot costume: a box torso, boxy helmet head, tube-like arms and legs, all styled with corrugated brown cardboard textures, foil accents, and duct tape details for that handmade craft look.

Now I'm working out the exact proportions -- deciding whether the kid's face peeks through a cut-out window in the head box or sits beneath it, then pinning down coordinates for feet, knees, hips, shoulders, and head box placement so the torso and helmet boxes line up naturally over the child's body.

I'm also mapping out the arms as cardboard-tube sleeves over the kid's real arms, held in a T-pose with gloved hands, and sketching hip-to-leg placement for the lower body.

Now sizing the whole costume: legs get box sleeves on the shins, overall width stretches to cover extended arms, and I'm adding an antenna with springs and bottle caps on top of the head, bringing total size to roughly [1.5, 1.55, 0.52] once depth from torso, feet, and chest panel details are accounted for. Then I start breaking the model into parts, starting with the kid's head and face.

Now I'm thinking through the humanoid rig and how to divide the costume into manageable groups — separating the kid's head/face/hair/jaw/neck from the limbs (pants, shoes, hands/fingers), and grouping the torso as its own box piece with the control panel, buttons, dials, tape, and straps.

I also want a headBox group for the box helmet with face window, antennas, ear bolts, and visor, plus a limbCostume group covering the cardboard/foil arm tubes, shin boxes, elbow joints, and bracers. For joints, I'm planning shoulder-elbow-wrist chains per arm with hand/finger digit joints for the mitten thumbs.

Settling on 5 digits per hand with 2 joints each, 10 joints per hand, 20 total, and starting to lay out the full joint hierarchy from hips up through spine, chest, neck, and head with positions and directions for a T-pose rig.

Now I'm figuring out the jaw hinge placement relative to the head geometry, checking that the head box dimensions and the kid's head sphere radius line up proportionally.

I'm adjusting the face window so it sits flush with the forward position of the kid's head, shifting the head center and box depth so the face isn't recessed oddly inside the box, then aligning the torso box top edge with the head box bottom so the neck fits naturally between them.

Now I'm placing the arm holes and shoulder joints at the torso box edges, roughing out shoulder-elbow-wrist positions for a stylized chunky arm proportion matching the kid's overall scale.

Deciding the kid wears a long-sleeve shirt rather than bare arms. Now I'm building the leg joint chains: hip, knee, ankle, and toe for each leg, positioning them down to the floor with shoe height accounted for and assigning parent-child relationships and leg roles to each joint.

For the geometry, I'm sketching shin boxes around the legs and shoe boxes around the ankles, sizing them so shoes touch the floor while shins stay above it, and checking the overall depth of the figure from head to the front of the shoes.

Now I'm working on the head and face: eyes, brows, nose, mouth, jaw as a separate piece for expressions, ears, cheeks, hair tucked under the head box but peeking through the window, plus an antenna with a spring and ball cap sitting on top, finalizing overall height around 1.55.

Then I'm setting up the skeleton hierarchy - neck and head joints, a hips-spine-chest chain for the torso, with the torso and head boxes riding their respective joints, and defining the arm chain from shoulder through elbow to wrist.

Now I'm extending the chain to the hand tip, with thumb and finger joints positioned for a T-pose with palms down, spacing index through pinky across the palm at different depths.

Total joint count comes to 42, which works. I'll skip rigging the antenna separately since it's rigid on the head, and no flap hinges are needed either. For the cardboard craft aesthetic, I'm defining a color palette with tan and dark cardboard tones, corrugation edge stripes, silver tape, duct tape grey, foil highlights, and marker colors for details.

Continuing the palette with button green, a cyan for the marker-drawn screen glow, skin tones with cheek blush, hair colors, blue shirt, jeans, white sneakers with a red sole, red glove, eye and iris colors, pink lips, and glue blob white for craft details.

Now I'm working through the cardboard-robot styling: corrugated ridges, torn and folded box flaps, crisscrossed masking tape, hand-drawn marker knobs, bottle-cap buttons, a bendy straw, a paper clip, and lettered labels like "ROBO" and a "MAX" name tag. Then I start assigning body parts, beginning with the kid's head (skull, face, eyes, hair, jaw) with its joint and bounding box setup, and I'm moving into the limb assignments next.

Now the torso box needs a chest panel with dials, buttons, screen, tape and name tag, plus a cardboard back-pack with foil tubes, with torn arm holes and spine/chest joints — budget 200. Then the head box needs a face window, cut flaps, and an antenna spring.

I'm also adding a hip belt with a bottle cap buckle to the torso box, and sizing the arm tubes to wrap around the kid's arm radius with upper arm and forearm sections spanning specific x ranges, leaving a gap at the wrist for gloves.

Now I'm cataloging all the mount points for the costume pieces: neck base, head center, face window, head box top/bottom, shoulder holes, elbows, wrists, knees, ankles, shin box edges, chest panel, backpack, belt line, and hip points.

For colors, I'm sticking with tan cardboard with lighter flap interiors, and thinking through how the face window should be built as a cutout framed by four strips rather than a solid panel with a hole. Similarly, I'm planning the arm holes in the torso as a solid wall with a dark torn-edge ring flange where the arm tube passes through, keeping construction simple for the builder.

Now I'm settling on a limited 24-color palette covering cardboard tones, tape and foil materials, marker colors, bottle cap colors, and skin and hair tones for the figure.

I'm still paring down the palette, trying to land on exactly 24 colors by cutting redundant shades like hairLight and skinShade while keeping the essentials: cards, tape, marker tones, skin, hair, shirt, jeans, and sneaker colors.

Now I'm checking the part budget totals to stay under the limit, trimming numbers down from 900 to around 860. Then I'm moving on to writing out the joint hierarchy with coordinates for hips, spine, chest, neck, and head.

Placing joint positions...

Now mapping out the kid's head: a chunky blocky skull with big front-facing eyes, ears at the sides, tousled hair blades peeking through the window, small nose, and an open grin with upper/lower jaw teeth. I'm positioning the neck and shirt collar around y 0.88-0.93 attached to the head group, and defining the face window so the kid's face shows through at the right depth.

With the eyebrows settled, I'm ready to write out the final JSON.

I'm planning the buildKidHead function, figuring out how to attach head geometry to the bone joint using model-space positions and defining the head's center and radius.

Now I'm calculating precise positions for facial features — eyes, sclera, iris, and highlight — by computing where each sphere's surface intersects with the skull given their offsets and radii. Then I move on to the jaw and mouth, working out the chin block's dimensions and where the lower jaw bone should sit relative to the skull's bottom curvature.

For the smile, I'm shaping a torus arc rotated 180° to form the lower half of a circle, positioning it so it sits flush against the face surface at the correct z-depth.

I'll build the lips as a chain of small spheres along a curved path computed from head coordinates, connecting them with capsules for a smoother mouth shape.

Now I'm placing upper teeth as small white boxes beneath the lip line, then working out the chin geometry as a sphere positioned to protrude slightly past the skull's natural curve for a chunky jaw look.

Continuing with the lower lip as a capsule chain sitting just below the upper lip, with a gap between them creating an open mouth. For the dark interior I'm defining a custom color and placing a thin plate behind the lips on the head bone, plus a flattened tongue sphere using the lips color.

Now I'm positioning lower teeth as small white boxes on the jaw, confirming the jaw hinge placement works fine since parts just follow the bone. For cheeks I'm working out thin disc geometry oriented along the surface normal, computing the normal vector from center to cheek position and solving for the z-coordinate using the sphere surface equation.

I'm computing the exact cheek position, then adding a helper that lifts points outward along their normal by a small offset to avoid z-fighting with the skull surface. I'm also checking that a low-poly faceted sphere's deviation from the true analytic surface stays small enough that a 4mm lift covers it, settling on 20x14 segments for the skull.

Still working out skull proportions...

Now I'm working out the eyebrow shape, debating whether inner or outer ends should sit higher to read as a gentle happy arch rather than angry, and positioning the brow arc along the head's curved surface near y≈1.14.

I'm realizing a single hair cap angled to cover the whole scalp would also cover down over the eyes, so I need to split it into separate back and front sections with different angular ranges to keep the hairline above the eyebrows while still covering the back and sides.

Placing the hair sphere around the head center with a slight offset, checking it stays within the head bounds. For bangs, I'm considering flattened cone shapes as blades draped over the forehead, oriented to follow the scalp's curve.

Working out the bang placement math: seven blades spaced across the hairline, each with a base point computed from spherical coordinates on the skull, and an apex direction blending a downward tangent with an outward normal so the bangs curve naturally off the forehead.

I'm checking the geometry against eyebrow and eye positions to make sure the bangs land just above the brows without covering the eyes, adjusting the hairline angle and blade lengths until the tips sit around y≈1.16.

I'll add a few extra cone shapes for stray hair tufts and a cowlick spike angled upward near the crown, plus some flatter overlapping cones for the main bangs. For color, I'm planning to keep the palette mostly in the hair tone but add a subtle darker highlight shade for some strands.

Now I'm working out the eyes: white sclera spheres squashed along z, positioned just proud of the head surface near the front, oriented so they face outward along the local normal direction.

Bumping pupil lift to 0.0145 fixes the hidden-pupil issue, and I'm placing a small white highlight sphere offset from center with its own lift so it reads above the iris. Now I'm working out the top eyelid as a thin curved capsule line arcing over the sclera, picking y-coordinates and lift values so it sits proud of the eye's curvature.

I'm outlining the upper eyelid as a thin arc sitting proud of the skin, then dialing back the sclera and iris proportions so the eyes read as cartoonish rather than bulging bug eyes, adjusting lift and scale values for a more natural front profile.

Working through the pupil and highlight placement to ensure the highlight sits just outside the iris surface while the pupil stays recessed slightly behind it, confirming the geometry lines up correctly. Then starting on the nose as a scaled sphere positioned on the head surface.

I'm recalculating the nose dimensions to keep the tip just under the maximum offset limit, settling on a smaller lift and radius so the front point lands around 0.177. I'm also deciding to give the nose tip a slightly pinker tone using the cheek color rather than pure skin color, and skipping nostril details for now before moving on to the mouth.

Now I'm mapping out the mouth geometry—placing corners, computing surface offsets for the smile curve, and planning small dark capsule shapes for corner dimples, then sketching the upper lip curve and teeth box dimensions and positions.

Placing seven teeth under the lip line, orienting each box so its depth aligns with the surface normal, and tuning the lift so teeth sit just proud of the skin while staying tucked behind the lip. Now I'm planning a dark interior plate to fill the gap between upper and lower teeth for mouth depth.

Since the grin was nearly closed, I'm widening the vertical gap to around 0.018 by redefining the upper lip height and recalculating where the teeth centers and bottoms fall relative to it, aiming for a more open, friendly expression.

Now I'm placing the lower teeth as a row of six small rectangles centered beneath the lower lip curve, then checking how the chin surface geometry recedes to make sure the lip sits naturally against the jaw.

Still working through jaw geometry...

Checking the teeth positions against the jaw ellipsoid surface at a few sample points, the values line up reasonably well. For the lip geometry, I'm placing the lower lip chain slightly offset from the jaw surface, lifted along the ellipsoid's approximate surface normal computed from the gradient.

Now I'm sketching the overall structure: a shared surface helper for both skull and jaw ellipsoids, with the skull as a sphere-like shape above and the jaw ellipsoid covering the lower face below the mouth. I'm verifying the seam where the jaw meets the skull at the sides stays consistent in width at the hinge point.

For the dark interior mouth plate, I'm positioning it just in front of the skin surface so it's visible through the gap between jaw and skull, checking the surface heights at the relevant y-coordinates to get the lift value right.

That's not quite working either. I'll try a chain of small dark boxes across the gap instead, like individual teeth segments, each sized to the local gap height and positioned against whichever surface sits forward at that point — or maybe just fill the gap with a tongue shape instead of dark boxes.

Adding neck geometry...

I'm adding small mouth corner markers, tiny freckle dots near the nose bridge, and defining the hair color palette with a main shade plus highlight and darker back tones. Then I'm setting up the jaw joint and bone hierarchy before working through the part-building function's parameters.

Writing head geometry code...

I'll clamp q so it stays stable near edges, then write a small helper that places a part at a surface point using its position and normal as direction, tagged to the bone. For axis alignment I'll allow overriding to "y" for disc shapes, and I'll add a chain helper that connects points with capsules for joints.

Now I'm tallying up the expected part counts across the skull, jaw, ears, eyes, brows, nose, freckles, cheeks, and mouth to sanity-check the build.

Adding skull, jaw, neck, ears, nose, cheeks and trimming freckles to 4 brings the total to 102, comfortably under the 120 budget. Now I'm working out the lip curve coordinates, using quadratic functions for the upper and lower lip shapes with six segments each for the capsule chains.

Placing the lower lip proud of the jaw surface with a slight lift, and positioning lower teeth just above it with their own depth and lift values. For the interior mouth pieces, I'm stepping across x-positions to compute heights between the upper teeth bottom and lower lip, deciding whether to anchor each piece to the skull or jaw bone based on whichever surface sits higher.

Still placing teeth...

Finishing lower teeth positions on the jaw, then checking the gap between upper and lower teeth stays positive across the curve. Then I'm placing a small flattened sphere for the tongue, anchored to the jaw just behind the lower teeth.

I need to make sure the tongue's front edge doesn't poke out past the teeth, so I'm adjusting its scale and vertical offset so it stays tucked slightly behind, letting the jaw surface itself hide the back portion.

Now I'm figuring out the mouth corners, computing marker positions along the skull using offset points near the lip ends.

For the hair, I'm working out the back cap sphere geometry's phi/theta ranges to make sure it covers the correct side of the head given the coordinate orientation.

I'm adjusting the back cap's theta angle to avoid overlapping the ear geometry, tightening it to 95° so the hair sits just outside the ear position.

Now I'm defining the front cap sphere geometry so it covers the top of the window, leaving the bare sides between ear and eye intact for sideburn cones.

Merging back and front hairline caps with overlapping radii, giving the back cap a darker shade while keeping the front lighter. Then setting up bangs as a loop over angle, length, tilt, and color data to build out each strand's direction vector.

Placing cowlick cones on top...

Placing more back and side tufts, angled downward-backward near the ear region, using five tuft positions at symmetric azimuths to fill out the hair coverage.

Now I'm adding sideburns in front of each ear, calculating base position on the skull at roughly 68° azimuth and elevation so they sit just forward of the ear, pointing downward along the cheek.

That brings my hair part count to 20 total: 2 caps, 8 bangs, 3 cowlicks, 5 tufts, and 2 sideburns. I'm also planning to add a highlight stripe color on a few bangs for visual interest, then moving on to positioning the eyes symmetrically with irises looking slightly forward and defining the lid outline as a small arc of points around each eye.

Now I'm working out the sclera and lid geometry, making sure the lid sits slightly outside the sclera outline, and adding a small outer lash flick extending outward and upward from the corner of each eye.

I'm also placing the eyebrows with three control points per side, giving them a slight tilt and hair-colored thickness, while checking they don't overlap too much with the hairline bangs above.

For the skull, I'll use a smooth sphere geometry rather than flat-shaded facets to avoid papercraft-style seams, skipping extra scaling since the mismatch is negligible. For the neck, I'm sizing a small cylinder to connect skull bottom to jaw, checking that it sits properly inside the jaw ellipsoid without poking through.

Now I'm adding a shirt collar using two small tori at slightly different radii and heights for a layered look, skipping the V-neck detail and extra flaps for simplicity. For ears, I'm placing scaled spheres on the head bone with a smaller inner disc sphere for the ear canal, carefully adjusting positions and scale so the inner piece stays just inside the outer ear bounds.

Now I'm setting up the color palette constants to use across the eyes, skin, hair, shirt, and other features for consistency.

I'm writing a helper function that places geometry parts onto the head bone using position, direction, and axis orientation, letting me construct eye pieces like the sclera with proper scaling and placement.

Now I'm figuring out the facial feature positions and dimensions—cheek discs using cylinder geometry oriented along the y-axis with small radius and thickness, then the nose as a scaled sphere positioned slightly forward on the skull surface, with a smaller tip sphere offset lower and further out to create the nose shape.

I'm placing freckle spheres symmetrically on both cheeks using small radius dots positioned slightly off-center, and building the jaw as a scaled sphere attached to the jaw bone for skinning.

Now I'm working out the interior teeth row, stepping across the mouth width to compute box dimensions between upper and lower jaw curves, sizing each tooth so they blend with the lips at the mouth edges while sampling depth against both skull and jaw surfaces to pick the correct z-position.

Still writing helper functions...

Checking the geometry so each hair cone's base sits just inside the scalp cap radius while the tip emerges outward, verifying this works for both back tufts near θ 78 and front bangs near θ 31 where the cap boundary differs.

Now setting up sideburns with mirrored angles for left/right symmetry, then defining the bang parameters as a list of angle, length, and sweep values, with sweep direction mostly positive for a side-swept fringe look across the forehead.

Moving on to the eyes, I'm placing white sphere eyeballs flattened slightly on one axis for both left and right positions, then adding iris spheres...

Checking that the iris size fits proportionally within the sclera bounds.

I'm working out the function signature for buildKidBody, and since I'm unsure whether a Ctx type is actually exported, I'll just define my own loose inline type covering the body, joints, parts, and mesh data instead of relying on an import.

I'm also sketching out the body layout using capsules and boxes positioned relative to the joints—rigid limb segments attached to each bone rather than smooth skinned sweeps—then mapping out the torso, hem, and waistband geometry with approximate y-coordinate ranges for the shirt and jeans.

Defining chest stub dimensions with shoulder ball joints, then setting up leg bone chains with hip, knee, and ankle positions and tapered thigh/shin capsules, plus shin boxes for pocket details.

Since most of the thigh is hidden under the torso box, I'm adding a rolled ankle cuff visible between y 0.085-0.125, deciding to rig it to the ankle bone for simplicity, then starting on sneaker geometry rigged to ankle and toe bones.

Splitting each sneaker into sole and upper sections: the heel/mid portion of the sole and upper attach to the ankle bone, while the front portion attaches to the toe bone, dividing roughly at z 0.09.

Still working out shoe geometry...

Still positioning sneaker parts...

Still defining arm geometry...

Working out palm geometry spanning roughly x 0.69–0.78, sizing it as a rounded box centered near 0.735 wide in z, and deciding to attach it to the wrist bone rather than the hand joint since the hand joint sits at the fingertip end. Also placing a lighter cuff band near the wrist transition into the sleeve.
